PullRequest.Title: agentHost: offer Context Size for extension BYOK models in Copilot sessions
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Fixes #333017

Extension models that publish a numeric `contextSize` enum in their `configurationSchema` (the shape Copilot Chat uses for its own models) now get a Context Size picker in Copilot agent sessions, beside Effort Level, in the chat view and the Agents window. Until now the BYOK bridge only carried `reasoningEffort`, so the SDK always ran these models against their full window. On a 1M-token model a long session re-reads close to a million cached tokens every turn; the extension can offer 200K, and the user should be able to take it.

The renderer's `listModels` forwards the schema's values, labels, descriptions and default as an optional `contextSizeOptions` on `IByokLmModelInfo`. The agent host turns that into the `contextSize` config property, and `synthesizeByokSessionConfig` registers the selected model with the SDK at the chosen size (`maxPromptTokens`, with `maxContextWindowTokens` shrunk to match), so compaction runs against that budget rather than the full window. A mid-session change re-registers the model through the existing `provider.sync` path before `setModel`; resume registers at the stored selection. A saved choice the model no longer offers falls back to the extension's default, never to an arbitrary number.

I first reached for the SDK's session-level `modelCapabilities` override, which looks like the obvious knob. It isn't scoped to a model: it survives `setModel` calls that omit it, so a 200K choice on one model would silently cap the next one. Per-session provider model limits don't have that problem, and the runtime re-reads them on `provider.sync` and on resume, which the new integration test pins against the bundled runtime.

The bridge field is optional on both ends, so a newer renderer with an older agent host (or the reverse) keeps today's behavior. Copilot's own models, `contextTier`, free long context and Effort Level are untouched.

One thing I deliberately left alone: the extension still receives `modelConfiguration.contextSize` from the renderer's global per-model setting, not the session's choice. The value is a prompt budget the SDK applies when it builds and compacts the conversation; the provider only sees the result, and no provider I know of acts on it. Threading it through would mean tracking per-session selections in the proxy for a field nobody reads. Easy to add if a provider turns out to need it.

Related: #340138 asks for the provider's whole `configurationSchema` to survive the bridge; this covers its `contextSize` slice explicitly rather than forwarding the raw schema. #329892 asks for the same knob via `chatLanguageModels.json`; not covered here.

### How to test

- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/copilotByokContextSize.integrationTest.ts` passes against the bundled SDK (1.0.23-preview.1 / runtime 1.0.99), as do the existing `copilotByokResponses` and `copilotByokSelectionIds` suites (6 passing).
- The BYOK handler, bridge registry, Copilot agent, session and launcher unit suites plus the chat model-configuration suites: 2,205 passing. `npm run compile`, hygiene, `npm run valid-layers-check`, `npm run check-cyclic-dependencies` and ESLint on the changed files pass.
- By hand: install an extension whose model publishes `contextSize` (numeric enum, `group: 'tokens'`), set `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`, start a Copilot agent session and pick the model. Context Size should appear beside Effort Level; with `--log trace` the agent host logs `Registering BYOK model <id> at context size <n>` and `Usage info: …/<n> tokens` on later turns.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Registering only the model's maximum prompt budget delayed compaction until the full advertised window, causing every later turn in long sessions to repeatedly serialize, transmit, and process a much larger prompt history than a user-selected smaller budget requires.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Long BYOK sessions on very large-context models incur increasing per-turn request bytes, token processing, and latency until the full advertised prompt limit is reached.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The session launcher now resolves an offered BYOK context size per session and registers the model with that bounded prompt/window limit; live changes re-register through the existing serialized provider.sync path before setModel, and resume uses the stored selection.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, synthesizeByokSessionConfig copied each BYOK model's advertised maxPromptTokens directly into ProviderModelConfig (base line 661), so the runtime's compaction budget could not reflect a smaller model selection. The added getByokSessionModelLimits path resolves the selected/default context size and lowers both maxPromptTokens and maxContextWindowTokens; the added bundled-runtime integration test demonstrates that these ProviderModelConfig limits become session.usage_info.tokenLimit and assistant.usage.maxPromptTokens at launch, after provider.sync, and on resume. Thus a long BYOK conversation that previously remained eligible to grow to the advertised 968K prompt budget can now compact at the selected 200K budget before subsequent turns.

Scenarios.Scenario: Renderer BYOK model discovery and propagation into the agent-host model catalog
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An extension language-model change is debounced for 500 ms, then renderer-local listModels completes before one model snapshot crosses IPC and the agent host republishes its catalog. Existing sessions are asked to sync afterward, but unchanged SDK provider configs are suppressed and are not on the catalog publication critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Push the full BYOK model snapshot from renderer to the agent-host process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One snapshot after each coalesced language-model/visibility/entitlement change; payload grows with BYOK models and their context-size enum metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snapshot IPC occurred, without context-size arrays in each model DTO.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Enumeration and snapshot delivery must finish before the new picker metadata is published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize changed provider/model registrations into each live SDK session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one effective provider.sync per live session per resolved-limit change; SDK-equivalent snapshots stop before IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing model metadata changes already triggered the same per-live-session sync attempt; this diff can make a context-size/default change alter the SDK config, but realistic schemas are stable and updates are debounced/deduplicated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs as asynchronous follow-up and does not block catalog publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of renderer language models and the small context-size enum per BYOK model; active-session follow-up scales with the number of live SDK sessions only when resolved provider limits actually change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer enumerations are serialized/coalesced by a Throttler. Per-session SDK syncs may run across sessions, while each session serializes its own sync queue; equality prevents boundary calls for label-only or otherwise SDK-equivalent updates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The node registry caches the serving snapshot and compares context-size values, labels, descriptions, and default structurally. Equal snapshots do not notify. The renderer event is debounced and channel publication is throttled/coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event debounce, snapshot structural equality, config equality, and per-session serialization are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension model counts and schema-change frequency vary, but context-size enums are picker-sized and model registration changes are infrequent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added metadata is bounded by model schema size, and existing coalescing/equality prevents repeated expensive synchronization for equivalent snapshots.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a Copilot agent session using a BYOK model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The launcher reads the cached bridge models, starts or reuses the shared loopback proxy, synthesizes providers/models with the selected context budget, then waits for this config alongside shell-tool and custom-agent setup before SDK createSession/resumeSession proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Bind/start the local BYOK loopback proxy used by SDK provider registrations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once on the first BYOK-enabled session for the launcher, then reused across warm launches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical lazy shared proxy startup was already required for BYOK sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold proxy start must finish before SDK session creation/resume; warm launches reuse the handle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or resume the SDK/runtime session with the synthesized provider/model config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK create or resume operation per session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK operation registered advertised full-window limits; the diff does not add another boundary call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the session launch critical path; context-size metadata only changes numeric model limits in its existing payload.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct BYOK models after provider-qualified deduplication and context-size choices per model. Synthesis is local and linear in models aside from tiny picker-array normalization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: BYOK synthesis, shell tools, and custom-agent preparation run concurrently via Promise.all. Concurrent cold launches share one proxy-start promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Bridge models are a synchronous cached snapshot. The loopback proxy handle is memoized across sessions and reused warm; there is no separate context-size cache because the session selection is part of the result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the launch call path, shared proxy memoization, deduplication, and concurrent preparation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual SDK launch duration is environment-dependent, but the changed local computation and payload are small relative to the existing launch boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff adds bounded local configuration work and lowers selected prompt limits without adding launch boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change a live session's BYOK model or Context Size selection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user action queues on the chat sequencer, resolves the current BYOK config, performs provider.sync only if the selected limit changes, then calls SDK session.setModel so the runtime re-reads that registration. Model-configuration refresh follows.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace SDK provider/model registration through rpc.provider.sync.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when registration is unchanged; one before setModel when a context-size choice changes. A rejected switch may enqueue one bounded restoration sync.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: setModel already attempted sync, but context-size choices did not alter registration, so an otherwise unchanged catalog usually stopped at equality without this IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: For a changed BYOK context size, this call is intentionally on the user action's critical path so setModel observes the new limit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply the selected model through SDK session.setModel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same setModel boundary and ordering existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the selection change is committed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh managed settings and SDK model list/current-model state after the switch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One throttled/coalesced refresh generation after model switching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing finally block already scheduled this refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after setModel and is not required for the switch promise to complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user-selected model change; the synchronized config payload contains the deduplicated BYOK model catalog, while effective boundary cardinality is one provider.sync plus one setModel for a changed context size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model changes for a chat are sequenced externally, and each session's BYOK sync uses its own queue. A pending selection is read when queued work executes, avoiding duplicate corrective syncs in normal success paths.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The previous registered config is retained per session. compose/merge structural equality skips provider.sync when the resolved registration is unchanged; stale selections fall back to a stable advertised default.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: config equality, queueing, and exact IPC ordering are directly visible and covered by tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider.sync latency depends on the bundled runtime, but the trigger is an explicit low-frequency user action and only one call is added when semantics require a new limit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The newly effective provider.sync is a bounded, required control-plane call for a changed context limit, coalesced against unchanged state and serialized with competing syncs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continue a long BYOK conversation after selecting a smaller context size
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each turn still crosses the existing SDK-to-loopback-provider and renderer LM API boundaries. The runtime now compacts against the selected maxPromptTokens, reducing history before later inference requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send BYOK inference requests through the local OpenAI-compatible proxy and renderer language-model provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing inference boundary per model request/turn; no additional request is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The runtime used the model's advertised maximum prompt budget, so long sessions could carry substantially more history on every later turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This remains the main turn critical path. A smaller compaction limit reduces request serialization, bytes, and provider processing on long histories.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Conversation history token count up to the selected budget; request bytes and provider token processing scale with retained prompt tokens per turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Turn execution concurrency is unchanged. Context-limit updates occur on the serialized control plane before subsequent model use.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new response cache is introduced. The selected limit is stored in session model selection and re-applied on launch, provider.sync, and resume; prompt-provider caching remains external to this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the integration test establishes that ProviderModelConfig.maxPromptTokens controls runtime tokenLimit at launch, after sync, and resume; prompt work scales with retained history.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact savings depend on conversation length, selected size, provider caching, and token pricing/latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: This is a concrete performance improvement, not a regression. The introducing commit for the old full-window registration was recorded through report_regression_fix.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 15 changed files and traced model discovery, launch/resume, live context-size changes, and long-turn inference. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold; the PR instead bounds long-session prompt work, and that regression fix was recorded internally.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
